key_decisions: No Foundry/Hardhat/RPC: tools/evm-harness (solc-js + EthereumJS) is the contract test runner, because offline byte-identical reproduction on a fresh clone is what makes results credible to an outside auditor.
TS-DIFF (packages/protocol reference vs deployed contract) is the highest-value suite; zero divergences is merge-blocking and any divergence is automatically Sev-1.

Harness discipline as flake control: fresh Chain per test (do not rely on snapshot/revertTo); assert on timestamp not blockNumber (warp approximates blocks as seconds/2); harness gasUsed is execution gas only, so it is a regression detector and NOT a price - real cost needs calldata + blob-fee model + testnet.
The harness runs Mainnet/Cancun, so ALL L2 behaviour (force-inclusion, sequencer, L1 fee) is testnet-or-above; a harness-only suite may not gate an L2-dependent promotion.
Zero flake tolerance and no retries at L0-L3 (deterministic by construction); max one logged retry at L4-L6.

Coverage: 100% line+branch on packages/protocol and on the immutable core, justified by ADR-010 (core unfixable in place) and by protocol being the TS-DIFF oracle. Circuits are NOT measured by line coverage - the metric is 100% claims.json negative-test coverage plus a clean circomspect.
Quarterly seeded-defect drill (20 defects, >=90% caught) replaces a mutation-testing tool; no such tool exists in the repo and none was invented.

ZK doctrine: positive tests prove nothing; Z2 negative/malformed-witness tests are mandatory and CI fails when a claim in claims.json has no negative test; circomspect findings >= Warning fail the build; witness generation is differentially tested against packages/protocol; Gate-2 rule that circuit results MUST NOT be presented as evidence of soundness.

Capability-absence testing is first-class: ABI allowlist snapshot (primary), denylist + PUSH4 bytecode selector scan + DELEGATECALL/SELFDESTRUCT opcode scan, storage-layout snapshot, negative-authority matrix, human review checklist - with six stated limits of the technique.
Mock verifiers (MockVerifierAlwaysTrue) are banned from any suite claiming a ZK property.

Guardrail escalation rule: any defect against a guardrail FR or a capability-absence assertion is automatically Sev-1 regardless of user impact, because TD-04 leaves no override to fix the consequence.

Test data: no real personal data in ANY environment including a developer laptop (CON-002), enforced by three build-failing CI scanners with no bypass; production notification/support stores may never be copied downward.

OPEN-02 (Gate-2 blocking) FR-004's 50%-per-region attestor share cap has no implementing mechanism; PersonhoodRegistry has a per-epoch count cap and no region dimension.

OPEN-03 (Gate-2 blocking) FeatureFlags.disable() is unconditional and unilateral; nothing prevents disabling a flag governing an open ballot or blocking execution of a passed proposal - which NFR-020 requires and CON-003 forbids having.
OPEN-04 (Gate-2 blocking) ADR-003 scopes the issuer nullifier per issuer under 1-of-N acceptance, so one human with two accepted credentials enrols twice and votes twice, contradicting FR-001/BR-006.
OPEN-05 (Gate-2 blocking) PersonhoodRegistry.spendNullifier is external with no caller restriction - any address can burn any nullifier and deny a citizen an action.
OPEN-06 (Gate-2 blocking) issuerSetValid() is advisory; enrol() never consults it, so a region can fall to a single state issuer and keep enrolling.
OPEN-07 FR-011's minimum-substance standard is a 280-character length floor, not a substance check (OI-09 open).
OPEN-08 FR-002/NFR-001 'better than chance' is not falsifiable as written; needs an adversary game with epsilon and sample size.
OPEN-09 No named QA Lead in Doc 02's roster; Doc 04 ownership resolves to the architect per CLAUDE.md. Doc 13 subsequently names Ji-woo Park as Test Lead - reconcile at Doc 04 v1.0.1.

OPEN-10 OI-05: Doc 13 records it as design-resolved by ADR-004 s2 (escalate to nearest ancestor meeting k>=1000). That resolves PUBLICATION scope; the open point is that escalation must never apply to ELIGIBILITY, or a ward election's electorate silently changes. TS-ADV-06/A-06.10 tests that boundary.
OPEN-11 (Gate-2 blocking) NFR-025 demands alternative inclusion <= 60 min; ADR-001 states L1 force-inclusion is 12-24 h. Irreconcilable as written.
OPEN-12 RegionRegistry.submitPopulation is onlyTimelock, so 'independent' population sources all arrive through one authority.
OPEN-13 OI-10 collusion bound unset, so NFR-001 has no pass threshold.
OPEN-14 NFR-004's 0.1% duplicate rate is not internally measurable by design; needs an out-of-band consented audited sample with a stated confidence interval.
OPEN-15 NFR-005's median cost per citizen governance action has no enumerated denominator.
OPEN-16 ADR-001 and ADR-002 both cite a non-existent 'ADR-017'; the sponsorship policy lives in ADR-014. [RESOLVED by engineer; ADR-017 minted in this session for nullifier derivation and adapters]
OPEN-17 packages/contracts has no package.json/test workspace although root package.json declares test:contracts - npm run verify silently skips all contract tests today.

Verified the claimed capability absences hold structurally (no admin/pause/proxy/upgrade/transfer; no delegatecall/selfdestruct/payable/fallback; ring buffers correct at the 64-insert boundary; no reentrancy exploit in Governor.execute) - where the absences fail they fail through AUTHORISED callers. critical_findings: C-01 RegionRegistry.sol:169 issueResidency has no caller authentication - attesterId is caller-supplied and struct Attester has no operator address. Anyone mints unlimited residency credentials, which is the Sybil boundary for join/endorse and the source of verifiedResidents().

C-02 Governor.sol:259/153/343 never bind partyRootAtSnapshot or the circuit's snapshotAt. Party.knownRoot is written and read by no contract; error JoinedAfterSnapshot() is declared and never thrown. Unlimited forged votes at any tier against an attacker-built tree.

C-03 Circuit/contract public-signal arity mismatch: residency_member declares 7 vs contract 6, tenure_member declares 6 vs contract 5. The dropped inputs are exactly nowTs and snapshotAt - the two the circuit comments say the contract must bind. test/fixture.mjs registers mocks at the contract arities so UT-0341 validates the mistake. No personhood_enrol circuit exists at all.

C-04 Party.sol:279-281 surgeActive subtracts before the guard that prevents underflow. The first membership decrease permanently bricks join, leave and propose with no recovery path. JS reference does not share the bug (live differential divergence); UT-0420's fixture is monotonic by construction so it cannot catch it.

C-05 PartyRegistry.sol:306-356 openForkPetition takes initiators and forkInitiatedAt from calldata; no fork-initiation state exists anywhere. FORK_MIN_INITIATOR_BPS and FORK_COOLING_OFF are dead constants.

C-06 Governor.sol:327-340 binds no relationship between a proposal's tier and what its callData may do. A tier-0 proposal (5% quorum, zero discussion, zero timelock) can call Party.dissolve(). The entire ADR-008 s1 tier table is bypassable.
high_findings: H-01 PersonhoodRegistry.sol:268 setSpenderAuthoriser is re-callable and self-authorises its argument, with no de-authorisation path - the timelock can become a universal nullifier burner in one call. The Doc 06 s5 defect-1 fix is INCOMPLETE one level up, and irreversible. UT-0325/0326 do not cover it.

H-02 Party.sol:268-285 surgeActive is O(n^2) over up to 512 storage samples (~130,800 iterations at the cap) and is called from join/leave/propose - a hard liveness ceiling, not the optimisation Doc 06 s7.4 and SDD s13 describe.
H-03 GovernanceRules.sol:96 casts quorum to uint16 and wraps at >=6.5536x turnout; governance.js:147 does not. The chain can record Defeated on a 660% turnout the client reported as passed.
H-04 PartyRegistry.sol:216-229 withdrawEndorsement requires no prior endorsement, no jurisdiction match, no known root and no anonymity floor - residents of any region can decrement any petition.

H-05 VerifierRegistry.sol:53-80 has no emergency retire; a circuit found unsound stays live 30 days. enrol/issueResidency/join/leave/withdrawEndorsement are ungated by FeatureFlags, falsifying both the FeatureFlags docstring and Doc 06 s6.

H-06 The published identityCommitment is a stable cross-context pseudonym (indexed in Joined and Enrolled), defeating the scoped-nullifier unlinkability claim; PartyRegistry.endorse publishes it and never reads it.
H-07 RegionRegistry root history is 64 INSERTIONS, not a time window - at SDD s7.6 scale a proof's root is evicted before the citizen can submit it, and the revert is the misleading InvalidProof.
H-08 No personhood_enrol.circom exists; CIRCUIT_ENROL is the root of every Sybil claim and its circuit is unwritten. Doc 06 s7.2 does not say so.
verified_clean: No admin/pause/proxy/upgrade/ownership surface: enumerated every external+public mutating function across all 9 core contracts.
Mechanical scan for delegatecall, selfdestruct, assembly, payable, receive() and fallback() across packages/contracts/src/ returns nothing.
No transferable membership, no balance, no weight field; vote can only += 1.
authoriseSpender is correctly restricted to spenderAuthoriser and unreachable by any other path (H-01 concerns the layer above).
Nullifier scoping is sound at every call site except execute (M-04): join/leave/endorse/withdraw/vote/propose/cancel all pin their scope, which is inside the nullifier hash.

All three root-history ring buffers behave correctly at the 64-insert boundary: no still-valid root evicted early, no evicted root left accepted, root 0 handled. The defect is the sizing policy (H-07), not the buffer.

Governor.execute is CEI-safe against re-execution; no reentrancy exploit found (re-entering finalize/vote/propose/execute is independently gated). The danger is what the call may DO (C-06, M-04), not the ordering.
_ceilMulDiv matches Math.ceil; RegionRegistry._sort and PersonhoodRegistry.issuerSetValid() are bounded and not attacker-influenced; FeatureFlags is one-directional as advertised.
packages/protocol has zero runtime dependencies and dep-guard layering passes.
